title: The Mills Brothers' audition on Duke's train
summary: Duke's manager discouraged him from hearing the Mills Brothers, who auditioned on the train, and another agent took them and made the money that should have been Duke's.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: You know, Duke should have had the Mills Brothers. The Mills Brothers gave him an audition on the train.
The Mills Brothers' father worked on a train, didn't he?
I don't know whether he worked on a train or not, but --
I think Harry Mills told me once about how -- I remember, the boys came -- they were just teen-agers, I guess, --
-- children, when they came up to the train and came in and auditioned for Duke on the train, right?

Yeah, and instead of -- Duke had another manager. He was smart. Duke didn't fool around. He didn't say -- as if to say he didn't have time to be bothered with kids, you know. And this guy encouraged him to saying that. And then he saw -- he took them to -- what's that big booking agent the Mills Brothers worked for first? Well, whatever -- he took them and he made them. He got all that money but it should have been Duke's property, see.
They were from what city? Do you remember?
No, I don't. I think Columbus, Ohio, or somewhere around that part. Yeah, that was -- they gave him an audition and --
